ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the primary spermatocytes of a certain animal, in some cells, fragment exchange occurred between two non-sister chromatids of a pair of homologous chromosomes, producing 4 types of spermatids, as shown in the figure. If among the spermatids produced by this animal, spermatids 2 and 3 each account for 4%, then what is the proportion of primary spermatocytes in which exchange occurs during meiosis?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the primary spermatocytes of a certain animal, in some cells, fragment exchange occurred between two non-sister chromatids of a pair of homologous chromosomes, producing 4 types of spermatids, as shown in the figure. If among the spermatids produced by this animal, spermatids 2 and 3 each account for 4%, then what is the proportion of primary spermatocytes in which exchange occurs during meiosis?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a primary spermatocyte, in which a pair of homologous chromosomes are represented in white and black respectively, and fragment exchange can be seen between two non-sister chromatids. The right side shows the 4 types of spermatids formed: spermatid 1 is an all-white chromosome, and spermatid 4 is an all-black chromosome, belonging to the parental type; spermatids 2 and 3 respectively carry black-white interlaced exchanged fragments, belonging to two complementary recombinant types. Reasoning: Let the proportion of primary spermatocytes in which fragment exchange occurs be x. Each primary spermatocyte in which exchange occurs forms 4 spermatids through meiosis, among which the type spermatid 2 accounts for 1/4 of the spermatids produced by that cell, and spermatid 3 also accounts for 1/4. The question stem gives that spermatids 2 and 3 each account for 4% of all spermatids, therefore x × 1/4 = 4%. Solving gives x = 16%.
